questions.question: The area of the largest triangle that can be inscribed in a semi-circle of radius 6 cm is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The area of the **largest triangle** that can be inscribed in a **semi-circle** of **radius r** is always **r²**.

Given **radius (r)** = 6 cm

⇒ Area = 6²

⇒ Area = 36 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the semi-circle (r) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd9d9c7e22aea64f8a15c726a676cf34ba245cf477ec67f5e9c88852e94e2300.png] 

For a triangle inscribed in a semi-circle to have the **maximum area**, its base must be the **diameter** of the semi-circle and its **height** must be equal to the **radius**.

⇒ Base of triangle (b) = Diameter of semi-circle = 2 × r

⇒ Base (b) = 2 × 6 = 12 cm

⇒ Maximum Height (h) = Radius of semi-circle = 6 cm

⇒ Maximum Area = 1/2 × Base × Height

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 12 × 6

⇒ Area = 6 × 6

⇒ Area = 36 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 36 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semi-circle

Any triangle inscribed in a semi-circle with the diameter as one of its sides is always a **right-angled triangle** (Angle = 90°).

Area and Perimeter of Semi-circle

Area = 1/2 × πr² and Perimeter = πr + 2r (where 2r is the diameter).

Maximum Area of Inscribed Rectangle

The largest rectangle that can be inscribed in a semi-circle of radius r has an area of **r²**.</p

questions.question: A sum of money, on compound interest, amounts to ₹578.40 in 2 years and to ₹614.55 in 3 years. The rate of interest per annum, in case of annual compounding, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **annual compounding**, the **amount** at the end of a year acts as the **principal** for the following year.

Interest for the 3rd year = Amount (3 years) − Amount (2 years) = ₹614.55 − ₹578.40 = ₹36.15

Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

R = (36.15 ÷ 578.40) × 100 = (3615 ÷ 57840) × 100 = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ¼%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 2 years (A₂) = ₹578.40

Amount after 3 years (A₃) = ₹614.55

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/632c4f7be57410cdc8df8dc0592afd07e2b25ebe6694747187e20d7b698e13be.png] 

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ A₃ / A₂ = [P(1 + R/100)³] / [P(1 + R/100)²]

⇒ 614.55 / 578.40 = 1 + R/100

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 1.0625

⇒ R/100 = 1.0625 − 1 = 0.0625

⇒ R = 0.0625 × 100 = 6.25%

⇒ R = 6 ¼%

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ¼%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Basics

Compound interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest. Formula: A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt.

Successive Growth

In annual compounding, the growth between any two consecutive years (Year n and Year n+1) is simply the annual rate R% of the amount at Year n.

Comparison with SI

For the first year, if compounding is annual, Simple Interest and Compound Interest on the same principal at the same rate are equal.

questions.question: The problem of myopia in human eye can be corrected by using:

options.text: a biconvex lens of suitable power
a concave lens of suitable power
a convex lens of suitable power

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a concave lens of suitable power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Myopia, also known as nearsightedness, is a common vision condition where close objects appear clear, but distant objects are blurry.
 
• This condition occurs when the eye is too long relative to the focusing power of the cornea and lens of the eye.
 
• As a result, light rays focus at a point in front of the retina rather than directly on its surface.
 
• A concave lens (diverging lens) is used to correct myopia by diverging light rays before they enter the eye, allowing them to focus on the retina.
 
• The power of the concave lens is chosen based on the degree of myopia, ensuring that the light is focused correctly on the retina for clear vision.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hyperopia (Farsightedness)**

 
 
• In hyperopia, distant objects can be seen more clearly than close ones.
 
• This condition is corrected using a convex lens (converging lens) to focus light correctly on the retina.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism**
 
 
• Astigmatism is a condition where the cornea or lens is irregularly shaped, causing blurred or distorted vision.
 
• It can be corrected with cylindrical lenses that compensate for the irregular shape of the cornea or lens.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia**
 
 
• Presbyopia is an age-related condition where the eye's lens loses its flexibility, making it difficult to focus on close objects.
 
• This condition is typically corrected with reading glasses or bifocals.

questions.question: The distance between the pole and focus of a spherical mirror, in terms of its radius of curvature R, is equal to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**R/2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The distance between the pole and the focus of a spherical mirror is known as the focal length (f).
 
• The radius of curvature (R) is the distance between the pole and the center of curvature of the mirror.
 
• The focal length of a spherical mirror is half of its radius of curvature.
 
• Mathematically, this relationship is expressed as f=(R)/(2)
 
• This applies to both concave and convex mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirrors**

 
 
• These mirrors curve inward like a spoon and can form real or virtual images depending on the position of the object.
 
• They are often used in applications like telescopes and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirrors**
 
 
• These mirrors curve outward and always form virtual, diminished, and upright images.
 
• They are commonly used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula**
 
 
• The mirror equation (1)/(f)=(1)/(v)+(1)/(u) relates the focal length (f), image distance (v), and object distance (u) for spherical mirrors.
 
• This formula is applicable to both concave and convex mirrors.

questions.question: What is the least positive number that can be added to 2488 so that it is completely divisible by 3, 4, 5 and 6?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of 3, 4, 5, and 6, which is **60**.

Divide the given number 2488 by the **LCM** (60).

2488 ÷ 60 → **Remainder** = 28.

Least number to add = **LCM − Remainder** = 60 − 28 = 32.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number = 2488, Divisors = 3, 4, 5, and 6.

**Formula:** Least number to add = **LCM**(divisors) − (**Number** % **LCM**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82992ea80af2c694f97883bc1634081110a6da397a4c7551b09251b2fb94d5f4.png] 

⇒ **Step 1:** Calculate the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of 3, 4, 5, and 6.

⇒ 3 = 3¹

⇒ 4 = 2²

⇒ 5 = 5¹

⇒ 6 = 2¹ × 3¹

⇒ **LCM** = 2² × 3¹ × 5¹ = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60.

⇒ **Step 2:** Perform division to find the current **remainder**.

⇒ 2488 ÷ 60 = 41 with a **remainder** of 28 (since 60 × 41 = 2460, 2488 − 2460 = 28).

⇒ **Step 3:** Find the number needed to reach the next multiple of 60.

⇒ Required Number = **Divisor** − **Remainder** = 60 − 28 = 32.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of LCM

A number is divisible by a group of integers if and only if it is divisible by their **LCM**. For 3, 4, 5, and 6, the combined condition is divisibility by 60.

Addition vs Subtraction for Divisibility

To make a number **N** divisible by **D**: subtract the remainder (N % D) or add (D − remainder).

Divisibility by 60

A number is divisible by 60 if it ends in 0 and the remaining digits are divisible by both 3 and 4.</p

questions.question: If the perimeters of two similar triangles ABC and DEF are 75 cm and 40 cm respectively, and if overline{BC} is 15 cm, then the length of overline{EF} is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **similar triangles**, the ratio of their perimeters is equal to the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.

Ratio of Perimeters = Ratio of Sides

75 ÷ 40 = 15 ÷ EF

⇒ EF = (15 × 40) ÷ 75

⇒ EF = 600 ÷ 75 = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of ▵ABC = 75 cm

Perimeter of ▵DEF = 40 cm

Length of side BC = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

If ▵ABC ∼ ▵DEF, then:

Perimeter of ▵ABC ÷ Perimeter of ▵DEF = AB ÷ DE = BC ÷ EF = AC ÷ DF

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/013fad8f1e93ee36e80a29679f53c39d50e3458c992bbdd3c7199edb7f5efef3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter(▵ABC) ÷ Perimeter(▵DEF) = BC ÷ EF

⇒ 75 ÷ 40 = 15 ÷ EF

⇒ EF = (15 × 40) ÷ 75

⇒ EF = 600 ÷ 75

⇒ EF = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the **areas** of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their **corresponding sides** or perimeters: Area₁/Area₂ = (Side₁/Side₂)².

Similarity Criteria

Two triangles are similar if they satisfy the **AAA** (Angle-Angle-Angle), **SSS** (Side-Side-Side ratio), or **SAS** (Side-Angle-Side ratio) criteria.

Linear Ratios

The ratio of any linear components (**medians, altitudes, angle bisectors, or circumradii**) of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their **corresponding sides**.</p

questions.question: Which of the following formulas is used to calculate the volume by volume percentage of a solution?

options.text: frac{{Mass of solute}}{{Volume of solution}} times 100
frac{{Mass of solute}}{{Mass of solution}} times 100
frac{{Volume of solute}}{{Volume of solution}} times 100
frac{{Volume of solution}}{{Mass of solute}} times 100

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Volume of solute / Volume of solution × 100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Volume by volume percentage (v/v %)** is used to express the concentration of a solution when both the **solute** and the **solution** are measured in terms of **volume**.
 
• The formula for calculating volume by volume percentage is:

 **Volume by Volume % = (Volume of solute / Volume of solution) × 100**
 
• In this formula:
 
 
• **Volume of solute** = Amount of substance dissolved.
 
• **Volume of solution** = Total volume after mixing solute and solvent.
 
 
 
• This method is commonly used for **liquid-liquid solutions**, such as **alcohol in water**.
 
• **Option-wise Analysis:**
 
 
• **Mass of solute / Volume of solution × 100** – Used for mass by volume percentage, not v/v percentage.
 
• **Mass of solute / Mass of solution × 100** – Used for mass by mass percentage.
 
• **Volume of solute / Volume of solution × 100** – **Correct**.
 
• **Volume of solution / Mass of solute × 100** – Incorrect formula.
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Volume of solute / Volume of solution × 100.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mass by Mass Percentage (w/w %):**

 **(Mass of solute / Mass of solution) × 100**
 
• **Mass by Volume Percentage (w/v %):**

 **(Mass of solute / Volume of solution) × 100**
 
• **Molarity:** Number of moles of solute dissolved per litre of solution.
 
• **Solute:** The substance that gets dissolved in a solvent.
 
• **Solvent:** The substance that dissolves the solute to form a solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Example:** If **20 mL** alcohol is mixed to make **100 mL** solution, then:

 **v/v % = (20 / 100) × 100 = 20%**
 
• Volume percentage is widely used in **pharmaceuticals, beverages, perfumes, and chemical industries**.

questions.question: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is thrown vertically upwards and rises to a height of 20 m. The approximate initial velocity of the ball is:
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Equations of Motion under Gravity:**

__
 
• The motion of objects under the influence of gravity can be described using the equations of motion.
 
• For an object thrown vertically upward, the final velocity at the highest point is zero.
 
• Formula: v² = u² + 2as
 
• Here, **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, **a** is acceleration (due to gravity), and **s** is the displacement.
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity (g):** The acceleration imparted to objects due to the gravitational force. SI unit: m/s². Dimensional Formula: [LT⁻²]. g ≈ 9.8 m/s².

**Calculation:**__

Given,

Mass of the ball, m = 0.5 kg (Not required for calculation)

Maximum height, s = 20 m

Final velocity at the highest point, v = 0 m/s

Acceleration due to gravity, a = -9.8 m/s² (negative as it is upward motion)

Using the equation of motion:

v² = u² + 2as

Substitute the given values:

0 = u² + 2(-9.8)(20)

⇒ 0 = u² - 392

⇒ u² = 392

⇒ u = sqrt{392}

⇒ u ≈ 19.8 {m/s}

**∴ The initial velocity of the ball is approximately 20 m/s.**

questions.question: {If } cos⁴ theta - sin⁴ theta = k, { then the value of } (1-k)/(1+k) { is:}
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Substitute a standard angle **θ = 60°** into the given equation.

k = cos⁴ 60° − sin⁴ 60° = (1/2)⁴ − (√3/2)⁴ = 1/16 − 9/16 = −8/16 = **−1/2**.

Now, calculate (1 − k) / (1 + k) = [1 − (−1/2)] / [1 + (−1/2)] = (3/2) / (1/2) = **3**.

From the options, only **tan² 60° = (√3)² = 3** matches this result.

**∴ The correct answer is tan²θ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cos⁴ θ − sin⁴ θ = k

**Formula Used:** a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) and sin² θ + cos² θ = 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9f521fcbec7efcf02cce49b7ca3b1814be1422bbc436eaa657bda42f9759941f.png] 

⇒ k = (cos² θ − sin² θ)(cos² θ + sin² θ)

⇒ k = (cos² θ − sin² θ) × (1)

⇒ k = cos² θ − sin² θ

⇒ 1 − k = 1 − (cos² θ − sin² θ) = (1 − cos² θ) + sin² θ = sin² θ + sin² θ = 2 sin² θ

⇒ 1 + k = 1 + (cos² θ − sin² θ) = (1 − sin² θ) + cos² θ = cos² θ + cos² θ = 2 cos² θ

⇒ (1 − k) / (1 + k) = (2 sin² θ) / (2 cos² θ)

⇒ (1 − k) / (1 + k) = sin² θ / cos² θ = tan² θ

**∴ The correct answer is tan²θ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Double Angle Identities

The term **cos 2θ** can be written as cos² θ − sin² θ, 2 cos² θ − 1, or 1 − 2 sin² θ.

Pythagorean Trigonometric Identity

The fundamental identity **sin² θ + cos² θ = 1** is used to simplify higher-power trigonometric expressions.

Half-Angle Relationship

The expression **(1 − cos 2θ) / (1 + cos 2θ)** is a standard identity for **tan² θ**.</p

questions.question: Subtract the sum of 2x - 3y + 7z and 4z - 5x from 13x - z.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find the **combined sum** of the first two expressions by adding **coefficients** of like terms: (2 − 5)x − 3y + (7 + 4)z = −3x − 3y + 11z.

Subtract this sum from (13x − z) by **changing signs** of the sum: (13x − z) + (3x + 3y − 11z).

Group and solve: (13 + 3)x + 3y + (−1 − 11)z = 16x + 3y − 12z.

**∴ The correct answer is 16x + 3y − 12z.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First expression (E₁) = 2x − 3y + 7z

Second expression (E₂) = 4z − 5x

Third expression (E₃) = 13x − z

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Step 1:** Calculate the **sum** (S) of E₁ and E₂.

⇒ S = (2x − 3y + 7z) + (4z − 5x)

⇒ S = (2x − 5x) − 3y + (7z + 4z)

⇒ S = −3x − 3y + 11z

⇒ **Step 2:** Subtract S from E₃.

⇒ Result = E₃ − S

⇒ Result = (13x − z) − (−3x − 3y + 11z)

⇒ Result = 13x − z + 3x + 3y − 11z

⇒ Result = (13x + 3x) + 3y + (−z − 11z)

⇒ Result = 16x + 3y − 12z

**∴ The correct answer is 16x + 3y − 12z.**

**__Additional Information__**

Like Terms

Terms that have the same **variables** raised to the same **powers**. Only like terms can be added or subtracted.

Subtraction of Polynomials

To subtract a polynomial, change the **sign** of each term in the polynomial being subtracted and then combine the like terms.

Algebraic Sum

The sum is found by grouping the **coefficients** of identical variables: a×x + b×x = (a + b)×x.</p

⇒ b : c = (2 × 2) : (3 × 2) = 4 : 6.

__
 
• Limestone (CaCO₃) decomposes into quicklime (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) when heated.
 
• This type of reaction is known as a thermal decomposition reaction.
 
• In a decomposition reaction, a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• Thermal decomposition usually requires the input of heat energy.
 
• Quicklime (CaO) is widely used in the construction industry and for making cement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Combination Reaction**

 
 
• Involves two or more substances combining to form a single compound.
 
• Example: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O (Formation of water from hydrogen and oxygen).

questions.question: Rama walks to her office 5 km away from home. In the morning, she covers the distance in 1 hour whereas, while returning home in the evening, she takes 15 more minutes to cover the same distance. Find her average speed (in km/h) during the two-way journey.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance covered in the two-way journey = 5 + 5 = 10 km.

Total time taken = 1 hr + (1 hr + 15 min) = 2 hr 15 min = 2.25 hours or 9/4 hours.

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 10 ÷ (9/4) = 40/9 km/h.

40/9 km/h = 4 4/9 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 4/9 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance from home to **office** = 5 km

Morning time (t₁) = 1 hour

Evening time (t₂) = 1 hour + 15 minutes = 1.25 hours

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = Total Distance / Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4fc5d897fbe0665210fca5b8f99eb7ce616e1f70e655fd3c82e6db3c6fe31371.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 5 km (going) + 5 km (returning) = 10 km

⇒ Total Time = 1 hr + (1 + 15/60) hr

⇒ Total Time = 1 + 1.25 = 2.25 hours

⇒ Converting 2.25 to a fraction: 225/100 = 9/4 hours

⇒ **Average Speed** = 10 ÷ (9/4)

⇒ **Average Speed** = (10 × 4) / 9 = 40/9 km/h

⇒ 40/9 = 4 4/9 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 4 4/9 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If an object covers two equal distances with speeds x and y, the average speed is given by (2 × x × y) / (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If an object travels at speed x for time t and speed y for the same time t, the average speed is (x + y) / 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.solution:

__
 
• The magnetic field strength in a current-carrying circular loop is **maximum at the center** of the loop.
 
• At the center of the loop, the magnetic field lines are **most concentrated**, leading to the highest field strength.
 
• As you move towards the periphery of the loop, the magnetic field strength **decreases**.
 
• The magnetic field strength at the center of a circular loop is given by the formula **B = (μ₀I)/(2R)**, where B is the magnetic field, μ₀ is the permeability of free space, I is the current, and R is the radius of the loop.
 
• This concept is based on the **Biot-Savart law** which describes the magnetic field generated by a steady current.

• **Biot-Savart Law**

 
 
• This law helps in calculating the magnetic field generated by a steady current.
 
• It states that the magnetic field at a point is directly proportional to the current and inversely proportional to the distance from the current element.
 
 
 
• **Right Hand Rule**
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor.
 
• According to this rule, if you point the thumb of your right hand in the direction of the current, the direction in which your fingers curl gives the direction of the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field Lines**
 
 
• These are imaginary lines used to represent the magnetic field.
 
• The density of these lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field.
 
• Closer lines represent stronger magnetic fields, while lines further apart indicate weaker fields.

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 20 days and B can do the same work in 15 days. B worked alone for 6 days and left. In how many days can A complete the remaining work alone?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Work** = LCM(20, 15) = 60 units.

Efficiency of **A** = 3 units/day and Efficiency of **B** = 4 units/day.

Work done by **B** in 6 days = 6 × 4 = 24 units.

**Remaining work** = 60 − 24 = 36 units.

Time taken by **A** = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** to complete work = 20 days

Time taken by **B** to complete work = 15 days

**B** worked alone for = 6 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Remaining Work = Total Work − Completed Work

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Work** (LCM of 20 and 15) = 60 units

⇒ **Work done** by **B** in 6 days = 6 × 4 = 24 units

⇒ **Remaining work** to be done by **A** = 60 − 24 = 36 units

⇒ Time taken by **A** alone = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of **A**

⇒ Time taken by **A** = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 days

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of time is x:y, the ratio of efficiency is y:x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed among workers in the ratio of the actual work done by them or their efficiencies (if they work for the same duration).

Fractional Method

Work done by **B** in 1 day = 1/15. In 6 days, work done = 6/15 = 2/5. Remaining work = 1 − 2/5 = 3/5. Time for **A** = (3/5) × 20 = 12 days.</p

questions.question: In which organism does cell division or fission lead to the creation of new individuals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unicellular organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Unicellular organisms are single-celled organisms that perform all necessary functions within one cell.
 
• Cell division in unicellular organisms, such as bacteria and protozoa, is typically asexual and occurs through processes like binary fission or budding.
 
• During binary fission, the cell duplicates its genetic material and divides into two equal-sized daughter cells.
 
• This type of reproduction is efficient and rapid, allowing for quick population growth under favorable conditions.
 
• Unicellular organisms do not require a mate for reproduction, which simplifies the process and ensures the generation of new individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multicellular Organisms**

 
 
• In multicellular organisms, cell division is used for growth, development, and repair, rather than creating new individuals.
 
• These organisms reproduce through sexual reproduction, involving the fusion of gametes (sperm and egg cells).
 
 
 
• **Mitosis and Meiosis**
 
 
• Mitosis is a type of cell division resulting in two daughter cells with identical genetic material, used for growth and repair in multicellular organisms.
 
• Meiosis is a specialized form of cell division that produces gametes with half the genetic material, essential for sexual reproduction.
 
 
 
• **Cell Cycle**
 
 
• The cell cycle includes stages of cell growth, DNA replication, and cell division, ensuring the proper distribution of genetic material to daughter cells.
 
• Regulation of the cell cycle is crucial for preventing uncontrolled cell division, which can lead to diseases like cancer.

questions.question: Which of the following is the specialised cell that conducts information via electrical impulses from one part of the body to another?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neuron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Neurons are the fundamental units of the brain and nervous system, responsible for receiving sensory input from the external world.
 
• They conduct information via electrical impulses, known as action potentials, throughout the body.
 
• Neurons connect with each other to form networks that perform various functions such as motor coordination, sensory perception, and cognitive processes.
 
• Each neuron consists of a cell body, dendrites, and an axon, which help in the transmission of electrical signals.
 
• The synapse is the junction between two neurons where information is transmitted from one neuron to another through neurotransmitters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleus**

 
 
• The nucleus is the membrane-bound organelle that contains the cell's chromosomes.
 
• It acts as the control center of the cell, regulating gene expression and mediating the replication of DNA during the cell cycle.
 
 
 
• **Dendrite**
 
 
• Dendrites are the branched projections of a neuron that receive electrochemical signals from other neural cells.
 
• They conduct the electrical impulses toward the cell body of the neuron.
 
 
 
• **Axon**
 
 
• The axon is a long, slender projection of a neuron that typically conducts electrical impulses away from the cell body.
